question: Is the key of a no-CoT brew lookup (the intermediate colour s1 on a correct h=2 item) carried by the J++ subspace (the 'global workspace') or outside it?

background.paper: Global-workspace / Jacobian-lens paper (anthropics/jacobian-lens): on two-hop factual prompts the J-space part of an intermediate's probe, swapped by a clamped coordinate swap, moves the answer in 61% of items vs 28% for the remainder, and the remainder's effect falls to 6% when the J coordinates are clamped; the J part explains ~10-15% of the probe's variance.
background.ours: exp15/exp16 (Qwen3.6-27B): token-lens key swaps (J++ included) +0.03-0.13 over the random null, difference-of-means +0.56-0.67 at layer 40; lens answer swaps succeed (0.72-0.89). exp14 (Gemma): J++ reads s1 at the final position at AUC 0.66 where a probe reads it at 1.00.

gemma.jpp: exp12's own J++ fit for the -it model, cache/exp12/lenses/jpp_64p.pt (64 prompts; layers 0-58 even, plus 15 and 45). Not koayon's Gemma lens: it is fitted on the base model and transferred worse in exp12 (eval_transfer_v1)

methods.swap: Clamped coordinate swap (exp17_swaps): for the pair V = [v(c); v(c')] at a layer, coordinates c(h) = V^+ h; with c0 from the clean pass of the same batch, h <- h + (c0 + alpha (sigma(c0) - c0) - c(h)) V at every J++-fitted block of a band and every window position. alpha = 1 exchanges the two coordinates; clamping to clean targets means later layers do not swap back.
methods.window: Brew primary: the start colour token through the last prompt token (after the rule table; an all-positions edit would also rewrite the table's rule lines). Secondary, test only: all positions. Factual positive control: every position after BOS (the paper's).

families.jpp: unit J++ vectors of the colour tokens: J_l^T (gain * W_U[' colour'])
families.dm_full: unit difference of means of the final-position residual, key colour vs the rest, on correct h=2/h=3 dev items (exp15's diffmeans direction; key = s_{h-1})
families.dm_jpart: dm_full's J++ part: non-negative gradient pursuit, k = 25 (the paper's multi-hop k), over unit J++ vectors of every readable token (a letter or digit; special tokens excluded)
families.ar_full / ar_jpart / ar_rem: Qwen only, layer 42: exp15's NLA reconstructor colour vectors, centred over the 10 colours and unit, split the same way

edit_kinds.swap: the family's own coordinate swap (natural size)
edit_kinds.matched: the family's swap rescaled per position to the norm of the full direction's swap (primary for J-part vs remainder: AGENTS.md's matched dose)
edit_kinds.null: a fixed random unit direction per (item, arm, layer) at the reference swap's norm
edit_kinds.clamp: optional: the colour pair's J++ coordinates held at their clean values (the paper's control)

methods.decomposition_chance_level: explained variance of 10 random unit vectors per layer under the same pursuit: the share of dm_full's variance a 25-atom J++ fit explains by chance

items.dev: exp11's single_test bank (250 per h; exp15's dev bank and exp12's Gemma gate): correct h=2 items with exp15's swap targets (exp15_edits.swap_targets, same seeds); difference of means from correct h=2/h=3 dev items
items.test: a fresh bank shared by both models: seed exp17_test_20261012, single_first format, 1200 h=2 eval items + 1 shot, unique against exp11's, exp15's and exp16's banks; written only after the lock
items.eligible: correct h=2 items (baseline argmax = gold) whose in-batch clean pass also gives gold and that have swap targets
items.factual: probe-swap.json (anthropics/jacobian-lens @ 581d3986, Apache 2.0, sha256 a0edd27c...): 90 two-hop prompts, raw text, no chat template; each word = its first token after a space; eligible = clean next-token argmax is the answer's token

outcomes.key arms: argmax over the 10 colour tokens: success T(s1') (the written colour was looked up), start_swap T^2(s1'), echo s1' (said, not looked up), unchanged gold, other
outcomes.answer arms: success a' (said), relookup T(a') (looked up again), unchanged gold, other
outcomes.factual: success = full-vocabulary next-token argmax is swap_answer's token
outcomes.collateral: probability mass on the 10 colour tokens; 'other' rate; dose = mean |delta| / |h| over the edit
outcomes.no_llm_judge: every metric is an argmax rate; no judged outputs

arms.posctl: per band (multi-layer) x alpha in (1, 2, 4): J++ intermediate swap, J++ answer swap (the paper's check that the effect is not just writing the answer), random null at the intermediate swap's size
arms.dev: per band x alpha (bands (1, 2, 4, 8), single layer (2, 4, 8, 16)): jpp and dm_full key swaps, each with its own null; Qwen layer 42 also ar_full and its null; J++ answer swap at the two smallest alphas per band; one alpha-0 arm (must change nothing)
arms.test: at the locked settings: jpp_raw, null_jpp, jpp_answer (at jpp's setting); dm_full, dm_jpart (matched), dm_rem (matched), dm_jpart_own and dm_rem_own (natural size, the paper's protocol), dm_rem_clamp (matched remainder, J++ colour coordinates clamped), null_dm, other_item (dm_full swap of an unrelated colour pair), jpp_at_dm (raw J++ at dm's setting); Qwen: ar_full, ar_jpart, ar_rem (matched), null_ar; all positions: jpp_raw_all, dm_full_all, null_dm_all

selection_rule: Per model and family (jpp, dm, ar): the dev (band, alpha) with the largest key-swap success minus its own null's success; within 0.01 of the best, the smaller alpha, then the band with fewer layers, then the earlier band. J-part / remainder arms use dm's setting (they are not selected on). Computed by exp17.py select; a human approves before the lock.

hypotheses.H1_positive_control: On the factual prompts, the J++ intermediate swap moves the answer to swap_answer more often than the null (the paper's effect reproduces with our lenses and swap).
hypotheses.H2_main: On the brew test items, the J-part of the key direction (matched dose) swaps keys at a rate different from the remainder's (matched dose). The paper predicts J-part > remainder; our prior (exp14 reads, exp15 lens writes) predicts remainder >= J-part, i.e. the key is outside the workspace.
hypotheses.H3_clamp: If the remainder swaps keys, clamping the J++ colour coordinates does not remove that effect (paper: 28% -> 6% on factual intermediates).
hypotheses.H4_dissociation: The raw J++ answer swap succeeds while the raw J++ key swap does not: the workspace carries the output colour but not the lookup key.

per_model: T1 dm_jpart - dm_rem success (paired by item): mean, 95% bootstrap CI (10k, items)
T2 each of jpp_raw, dm_full, dm_jpart, dm_rem, dm_jpart_own, dm_rem_own, dm_rem_clamp (and Qwen ar_full, ar_jpart, ar_rem) vs its null: success difference, one-sided bootstrap p, Holm within model
T4 jpp_answer success - jpp_raw success (paired): CI
confirmatory_tests.reading: 'Key in J++ space' needs T1's CI above 0 and dm_jpart above its null; 'key outside J++ space' needs T1's CI below 0 and dm_rem above its null; otherwise inconclusive. Also reported: J-part and remainder gains as fractions of dm_full's gain, with doses.

power: Expected eligible test items: Qwen ~860 (h=2 dev accuracy 0.764), Gemma ~1100 (0.928). At n=860 a rate's SE is <= 0.017; paired differences of ~0.06 are resolvable.

stop_rules.K0: exp17.py check fails (trial path, hook numbering, or dev accuracy vs exp11/exp12): stop that model.
stop_rules.K1: The positive control's best J++ intermediate swap gain over its null is < 0.15 on a model: report it and ask before reading that model's brew J++ results as a test of the paper's claim.
stop_rules.K2: dm_full's selected dev gain over its null is < 0.10 on a model: the decomposition has nothing to split under this protocol; stop and ask (do not switch protocol unasked).
stop_rules.zero_arm: the alpha-0 arm must reproduce the clean outcome on every eligible dev item

deviations_from_paper: brew lookup keys, not factual intermediates (the factual set is run as the positive control)
difference-of-means key direction instead of a logistic probe (exp15's best writer; one vector per colour)
J++ lenses instead of the paper's J-lens; Gemma's J++ fit has only even layers (and 15, 45), so its bands edit about every other block
brew window starts after the rule table (all positions run as a secondary test arm)
matched-dose J-part/remainder is primary; the paper's natural-size swap is reported alongside

run_plan.order: Qwen then Gemma, never together on the GPU
run_plan.check_in_1: check, prep (decomposition stats), positive control, both models
run_plan.check_in_2: dev grid both models, select, proposed lock (human approval)
run_plan.check_in_3: lock, test bank, test arms both models, report and figure
run_plan.stages: EXP17_MODEL=<m> exp17.py baseline:dev check prep posctl | dev select | baseline:test test; exp17.py bank once after the lock
